newsitem.title: USA: Fitch upgrades $81.3 mln of Maine Turnpike revs.
newsitem.headline: Fitch upgrades $81.3 mln of Maine Turnpike revs.

text.p: Fitch Investors Service on Monday said that it had upgraded to A-plus from single-A a total of $81.3 million of revenue bonds issued by the Maine Turnpike Auhtority.
The rating agency also assigned its A-plus rating to about $50 million of revenue bonds slated for sale on February 11 through a syndicate led by Bear, Stearns & Co.
Fitch said that it the Authority had proven itself to be a quality organization able to fulfill the needed rehabilitation of the turnpike while achieving conservative financial operations.
It also cited the turnpike's low rates, well-though-out capital plan and the lack of competing routes.

Authority funding for a potential project to widen roads would not start until at least 2002, and with the lowest rates in the nation and strong management, the Maine Turnpike should have the ability to finance a well-conceived construction program, Fitch said. It added "Sensitivity analysis suggest that rates can be raised over 200 percent without diminishing returns in revenue collections."
